title: Trellis couching
subtitle: A grid of crossed laid threads tied down at every intersection
excerpt: Trellis couching lays two sets of parallel threads at right angles to form a grid, then ties each intersection with a small cross stitch or diagonal stitch to hold the grid flat.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), couching chapter. Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), trellis stitch entry.
heroPrompt: Trellis couching filling a leaf shape on linen, grid of threads tied at each intersection with tiny cross stitches, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Trellis couching works in three stages: lay horizontal threads across the shape, lay vertical threads over them, then tie every intersection. The tying stitch is usually a small diagonal stitch or a cross stitch that pins the two grid threads together at each junction.

items.label: Laid threads
items.value: Perle cotton no. 8, or 2 strands of stranded cotton

items.label: Tying thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands, contrasting colour for a decorative effect

content.text: Lay horizontal threads across the shape at even spacing of 4 to 6 mm, anchoring each thread at both edges.
Lay vertical threads over the horizontals at the same spacing, crossing at right angles.
Tie each crossing point: bring the needle up beside it, make one small cross stitch over the crossing, and go back into the fabric.
Work across all intersections in rows to keep them evenly placed.

items.cause: Horizontal and vertical threads not kept at equal tension.
items.fix: Anchor each thread at the fabric edge before moving to the next. Do not pull tightly.

items.cause: Working in an irregular order across the intersections.
items.fix: Work across each row from left to right before moving to the next row.

content.text: Trellis couching fills large shapes in Jacobean and crewelwork with an open decorative grid. It is much lighter than satin and adds visual interest without hiding the fabric ground. Pattern couching varies the tying stitch to make the grid itself a design element.
